hardware.name: NVIDIA DGX Spark
hardware.note: torch.cuda.get_arch_list() on this part returns sm_80/90/100/110/120 -- nothing is built for 12.1. Documented consequences on vLLM specifically: FLASHINFER_CUTLASS for NVFP4 MoE was removed on sm_121 'and it costs 13%'; HUMMING cannot initialize; VLLM_CUTLASS and FLASHINFER_TRTLLM fail with 'kernel does not support current device'. That gap is the prize.

substrate.why: vLLM on this fleet is a pip wheel with precompiled CUDA extensions (_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so, _flashmla_C.abi3.so, ...). Nobody has built it from source on aarch64/GB10, so there is no vendored tree to edit. Submissions are Python patches applied over the installed wheel.

wheel.note: Pinned exactly. A different wheel is a different substrate and its scores are not comparable.

substrate.mechanism: A submission is a directory under patches/<name>/ containing sitecustomize.py. It is put on PYTHONPATH for the candidate arm only, so it applies at interpreter startup and therefore reaches vLLM's spawned engine and worker processes -- which a post-import monkeypatch would not. Precedent: bench/patches/laguna-int4 on howtospark forces the Triton MoE path over Marlin in four lines.
substrate.outOfScope: CUDA kernels in csrc/. Reaching them needs a from-source vLLM build for sm_121, which does not exist yet on this hardware and is tracked as its own milestone -- it is also what would unlock recovering the documented 13%.

clustered.why: The pinned 0.26.0 wheel stalls on the 3rd-4th request of every multi-node boot -- a vLLM shm_broadcast deadlock, reproduced on two models and with both executors. The recipe's own image does not stall and IS cross-boot deterministic once the B12X MoE kernel is off. Clustered targets therefore pin the image; single-node targets keep the wheel.
clustered.note: A different substrate, so scores are NOT comparable with the 0.26.0 wheel. That is already the rule for a different wheel; an image is the same situation.

requiredEnv.VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE_why: MANDATORY. With it at 1 the same prompt returns three different answers in one boot. With it at 0 every run agrees and agreement survives a restart. This single variable was the whole non-determinism.
requiredEnv.NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX: DERIVED PER NODE -- see harness/gid_index.sh. It is 3 on one node and 5 on the other; a shared value points at an IPv6 GID on one of them and ibv_modify_qp fails INIT->RTR.
requiredEnv.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT: a host mount shared across boots

forbidden.--kv-cache-memory-bytes: Skips memory profiling on this build, and the first FP8 GEMM then dies with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS. Use --gpu-memory-utilization instead.
forbidden.--max-num-seqs 1: Does not boot on this build. It is also not needed -- see measurement.serialRequests.

evidence.stability: 8 serial requests, prompt lengths 115-2225 tokens, all returned in 2-4 s. The 0.26.0 wheel fails on request 3-4 after every boot.
evidence.determinism: One prompt, 3 serial requests, 2 separate boots sharing one VLLM_CACHE_ROOT: 6/6 byte-identical (01ba594f606e7c1d).

clustered.entrypointNote: A generic wrapper: it sets PATH and the cache directories, then runs `vllm "$@"`. Despite the name it is not model-specific.
clustered.requiredEnvValuesNote: Applied to every arm by the harness, before the target's own env. A target cannot opt out of these -- VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=0 is the reason this substrate is deterministic at all.
clustered.dockerFlagsNote: --gpus all is not optional and is easy to omit: without it the container starts, and vLLM fails with 'Failed to infer device type', which names nothing useful. --ipc host and --shm-size 64gb matter because vLLM's message queue lives in shared memory.

editableSurface.rule: patches/<name>/**. Nothing else may differ between the arms: same wheel, same model file, same serve arguments, same environment apart from PYTHONPATH.
editableSurface.enforcement: The harness builds both arms from the target's own serveArgs and diffs the wheel version and model sha256. A submission that changes the serve command is changing the measurement, not the engine.

gates.rule: Wheel version, model file sha256 and serve arguments are byte-identical between arms. Only PYTHONPATH differs.
Candidate output is byte-identical to the baseline arm on the target's prompts, at batch 1, warm, under the pinned serve config.
On prompts generated fresh from a random seed: output identical AND the speedup reproduces within tolerance.
gates.whySpeedupToo: THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS HERE, and it is stricter than the llama.cpp arena's gate 3. There, the editable surface is CUDA kernels, so a submission physically cannot memoize a response. Here the submission is arbitrary Python: a patch could cache completions keyed on the prompt and return byte-identical tokens at absurd speed, passing gates 1, 2 and 4 cleanly. Freshly generated prompts break that -- a cache cannot hit an input nobody has seen -- but only if the held-out arm is TIMED as well as compared. Identity alone would let the cheat through.
gates.toleranceNote: The held-out decode speedup must be at least this fraction of the claimed speedup's excess over 1.0. A real engine-level win generalizes to unseen prompts; a lookup table does not.

gates.rule: score > the current leaderboard score for every target claimed.

scoring.pairing: Paired ratios, arms alternating in one session on one node.

pinnedServeConfig.why: vLLM is only cross-boot deterministic under a pinned config, and gates 2 and 3 compare a baseline server against a candidate server -- two processes. Without the pins the gate fires on boot noise instead of on the patch. This is the one structural difference from the llama.cpp arena, where an ordinary serve command is already cross-boot identical.
pinnedServeConfig.measured: 2026-07-28, Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 on vLLM 0.26.0. A single-short-prompt probe was identical across three boots with cudagraphs on AND with --enforce-eager, so capture is not the cause and the arena does not pay eager execution. But a wider FOUR-boot run over four prompts corrected that picture: the first boot against a cold VLLM_CACHE_ROOT differs on every prompt, and even among warm boots identity is PER-PROMPT — three of four were rock stable (including a 6,863-token one) while a 1,715-token prompt flipped between two hashes. Not a length effect; a numerical knife-edge on one input, same family as batch size flipping the argmax at n=2.
pins: --max-num-seqs: pin it, but the VALUE is substrate-specific. On the wheel it is 1. On the clustered image 1 does not boot, so it is 6 -- and that is safe, because what breaks token identity is CONCURRENCY, and the harness never sends more than one request at a time. See measurement.serialRequests. Measured cross-boot identical at 6, serial.
--kv-cache-memory-bytes  (so the KV pool is not sized from profiled free memory, which changes block count and therefore attention tiling)
consequences: The first boot against a cold compile cache is discarded, exactly as the first request after a server start is discarded. Same rule, one level up.

Prompts are SCREENED for cross-boot stability when the baseline is recorded, and unstable ones are excluded from the gate and recorded in goldens.json. A prompt whose argmax is a coin flip would fail honest submissions at random.
A target needs at least two surviving prompts. One is too weak to catch a kernel that changed behaviour on a different shape.

determinism.batchSize: 12/12 identical at batch 1 warm; n=2 -> 2 distinct, n=6 -> 5. Any batching breaks token identity, so the ranked track is serial.
determinism.crossBoot: Per-prompt, under the pinned config and a warm cache. Not global — see pinnedServeConfig.measured. This is why the baseline screens prompts instead of assuming them.

thermalGate.note: The Spark idles ~43 C and a measured arm heats it ~10 C, repeatably. mlxfast's fixed 40 C is unreachable here.
thermalGate.whyRelative: An absolute ceiling assumes a fixed idle floor and the floor drifts. Measured 2026-07-29: the same node, verifiably idle, sat at 52 C while nvidia-smi ALSO falsely claimed 96% utilisation -- a 46 C ceiling taken from yesterday's 43 C idle then waits forever. maxStartTempC is kept only as the fallback when nvidia-smi reports no temperature at all.
thermalGate.multiNode: Runs on EVERY node before an arm starts. One hot worker makes a paired ratio meaningless, and it is the node nobody is watching.

multiNode.why: Greedy token identity DOES survive the NCCL collective. Measured 2026-07-29 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP2 across two Sparks: two separate boots, same pinned config, warmup discarded, 4/4 prompts byte-identical. This is the property the whole cheap gate rests on for any clustered target -- and it is a property of the collective, not of a model, so one measurement settles it for every multi-node target here.

measurement.transport: NCCL over RoCE (NET/IB, 2 virtual devices at 200 Gb/s), NOT sockets
measurement.scope: Two boots at 8192 context, not 1M, and not across a reboot of either node. Enough to stop treating multi-node as unrankable; NOT enough to skip the per-prompt stability screening the baseline command already does.

requirements: Launch the cluster over real OpenSSH, never a Tailscale SSH session. tailscaled does not run PAM, so pam_limits never fires and every raylet inherits memlock=8MB, which silently forces NCCL onto TCP sockets even when the root memlock fix is correctly applied. Assert `ulimit -l` is unlimited on EVERY node from inside the launch script.
Assert NCCL actually chose NET/IB and not NET/Socket. The socket fallback is silent, it still serves, and a paired ratio measured over sockets is not the recipe's hardware.

Pin VLLM_HOST_IP per node. /etc/hosts on this fleet maps each hostname to 127.0.0.1 BEFORE its ConnectX address, so anything resolving its own hostname binds loopback and the peer gets 'connection refused' to 127.0.0.1 -- which reads like an interconnect fault and is not one.

Put /usr/local/cuda/bin AND the venv's bin on PATH, by PREPENDING to the inherited PATH. FlashInfer JITs its kernels, so vLLM's has_flashinfer() is False without nvcc and the DSv4 decode kernel disappears; the build then shells out to ninja, which lives in the venv.
Every node passes the thermal gate and is verified idle before an arm starts -- the worker is where somebody else's job hides.
The candidate tree is synced to every node before its arm. A worker still on the base build measures a mixed cluster and produces a plausible number rather than an error.
multiNode.intent: Multi-node IS in scope for this arena -- plenty of Spark owners have two or more, and the clustered recipes are the ones that most need kernel help.

fleetBlocker.scope: EVERY multi-node target on this fleet, not one model. No TP2 target can hold a multi-boot baseline until it is fixed.
fleetBlocker.what: Under TP2 across two Sparks, requests stall indefinitely at random. Both worker ranks sit in multiproc_executor.worker_busy_loop -> dequeue -> acquire_read waiting for a command, and the driver sits in step_with_batch_queue -> get_response -> dequeue waiting for a response. All three are READERS on vLLM's shm_broadcast queue and nobody is writing. The 100% CPU with GPUs at idle wattage is shm_broadcast's spin-poll, which is why this looked like an NCCL collective hang for two days.
fleetBlocker.isolated: It is NOT DeepSeek. Reproduced on Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 (21 GB, no sparse MLA, no flashinfer overlay, no vendored kernel): warmup returned in 1 s, request 1 passed, request 2 with an ~800-token prompt hung for the full 300 s. Reproduce with harness/tp2_isolate.sh -- 2-minute boots instead of DeepSeek's five, which is the difference between a tractable bug hunt and an untractable one.
ruledOut: The interconnect. Raw TCP over the direct 200G link measured 1561 MB/s DURING a hang.
RoCE GID churn. Fixed separately by pinning NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f1; the stall persists with zero GID warnings.
NCCL entirely. No rank is in a collective in any stack dump.
Async scheduling. --no-async-scheduling is now set and the stall persists.
Kernel JIT. A 37-minute hang logged zero JIT events.
Prompt shape. A 64-token prompt that decoded at 26.5 tok/s hung on a later boot; the stall point moves between runs.
fleetBlocker.nextStep: Chase it on the 21 GB reproducer. Suspects in order: VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB (the stall correlates loosely with prompt size, and that knob sets the remote chunking), then the local-vs-remote reader accounting in shm_broadcast (a writer waits for ALL readers to set a read flag, and a miscounted reader would hang exactly like this), then vLLM 0.26.0 upstream issues for the same signature.
fleetBlocker.howResolved: Clustered targets pin the image substrate instead of the 0.26.0 wheel. The stall is a 0.26.0 defect; it is still worth reporting upstream, but it no longer blocks the arena.

measurement.serialRequests: ONE request in flight is the requirement. --max-num-seqs 1 was belt-and-braces and it does not boot on the clustered substrate. It is not needed: the harness sends one request at a time, so every forward pass has batch 1 whatever the ceiling says. Measured 2026-07-30 at --max-num-seqs 6, serial: byte-identical across two boots. What breaks token identity is CONCURRENCY (n=2 -> 2 distinct outputs), and the harness never creates any.

policy.optimizationVsRecipe: Optimizations preserve output and get the cheap gate. Changes that alter output (precision, quantization, sampling, speculation) are a new RECIPE on howtospark.com, not an arena submission, and need eval evidence.
policy.configVsEngine: Tuning serve FLAGS is a recipe, not a submission. This arena ranks changes to what the engine DOES with a fixed config -- dispatch, kernel selection, memory layout, scheduling.
policy.publicWeights: EVERY target must point at weights a contributor can DOWNLOAD. No target may require someone to produce their own quantization. Same rule as the llama.cpp arena, and for the same reason: a download barrier in front of the arena costs more than any kernel win inside it.
policy.publicWeightsEnforcement: A target declares weights.hfRepo and weights.public. The harness refuses a target with no weights block. Verify with the HF API that the repo is neither gated nor private.
